transcript.content: Hello. What brings you in to see me today?

Well, honestly, I’m just... I’m so exhausted. I’m here because it’s been a full year of this, and it is completely wearing me down. 

You see, I’m a phlebotomist, so I draw blood all day. I know how the system works, I know how the tubes are routed to the lab, and I know exactly how the charts are updated in the electronic medical records. And for the past twelve months, I have been trying—literally trying everything I can think of, making phone calls, tracking timestamps—to prove that someone inside the clinic system is intentionally changing or holding back parts of my dad’s lab results. 

I was looking right at the screen when his initial metabolic panels came back, and I saw the raw values. I know what they were. But then later, the official chart was completely different. Certain markers were just gone or altered to look normal. And no matter how many doctors I talk to about it, or how many times my own family members tell me to just let it go and that his numbers are fine, I *know* what I saw. The finalized chart does not match the initial data, and nobody will investigate it. They keep telling me I'm just stressed or that I misread the screen, but I do this for a living! I know someone is manipulating his file, and trying to get anyone to just look at the discrepancies and listen to me is... it's just draining the life out of me. I can't just pretend it's fine when I know they're hiding something about his health.
Have you ever heard voices, sounds, or whispering that other people couldn't hear?

Voices? No. No, absolutely not. I mean... I know exactly why you're asking that, because when you tell people that official medical records are being actively altered, they immediately jump to, 'Oh, she must be hearing things, she must be losing her grip.' But I don't hear whispering or voices or... or anything like that. 

The only things I hear are the actual, real sounds happening in the clinic, you know, the hum of the centrifuges spinning down the gold-top tubes, or the overhead paging system, or the phones ringing off the hook at the front desk. I am completely, one-hundred-percent grounded in reality, which is exactly why this whole situation with my dad's chart is so incredibly frustrating to me. I'm not talking about some... some phantom voice whispering in my ear; I am talking about raw, numerical data that I saw with my own two eyes on a high-definition monitor at workstation number four. 

I don't need to hear voices when I have actual visual proof of what the metabolic panel originally said before it was scrubbed. Well, proof that they keep erasing and denying, anyway. But no, to actually answer your question, I don't hear sounds that aren't there. I'm not hallucinating. I just see what *is* there, and I see what they are trying so hard to hide from me, and nobody will just sit down and look at the screen with me to see it for themselves.

Oh, no, no, it’s not like that at all. I know what you’re getting at, but it’s really just this one specific situation. People assume that because I’m so focused on getting to the bottom of this, my whole life must be falling apart or I must be suspicious of everyone around me, but that is completely untrue. 

Outside of this entire nightmare with the dispute about my dad’s records, my life is completely normal. I still go to every single one of my phlebotomy shifts—I usually work the early block, and I haven't missed a single day. I clock in, I do my job, I prep my tray, I draw the blood, and I am completely professional with my patients and my coworkers. I don't have any issues with them. Nobody at work is out to get me, and I don't think anyone there is doing anything wrong, except for whoever is touching that specific electronic record. 

And at home, it's the same thing. I pay my bills on time, my water and electric are never late, I take care of myself... I do my grocery shopping on Sundays, I keep my apartment clean, I make sure my scrubs are washed and ironed for the week. I manage all my normal day-to-day responsibilities without any problem whatsoever. I'm a fully functioning adult! I'm not sitting around paralyzed by paranoia or thinking my landlord or the cashier at the grocery store is part of some grand scheme. It's literally just this one, specific, undeniable issue with the clinic system and my dad's chart. Everything else in my life is totally fine and completely manageable, which is why it’s so insulting when people treat me like I’ve lost my grip on reality just because I won't drop this one very real thing.
Do you have any chronic physical health conditions or medical illnesses?

Physical health? No, I don't have any medical conditions like that. I mean, honestly, I'm perfectly healthy. I don't have high blood pressure, no diabetes, no thyroid issues... I don't even get seasonal allergies, really. I take a multivitamin in the morning, sometimes a little vitamin D in the winter when it gets dark so early, but that's it. I don't take any prescription medications. 

I actually had a full physical myself just a few months ago, right before the clinic switched over to the new insurance provider for the staff, because I wanted to make sure everything was documented under the old system just in case... well, you know, just to have a clean baseline. And my labs were completely pristine. My fasting glucose was perfect, my lipid panel was well within normal limits, my CBC was completely unremarkable. 

So, physically, I am fine. Which is honestly a blessing, because if I were dealing with some kind of chronic illness on top of the sheer exhaustion of trying to get someone to pay attention to what's happening with my dad's chart, I don't know how I would manage. It takes so much energy just tracking the digital footprints of his records and calling the lab supervisors and trying to get a straight answer out of the IT department. If I had, you know, chronic pain or something, I wouldn't have the stamina to keep pushing for the truth. But no, my body is holding up just fine. It's just my patience that's completely worn out. I am physically as healthy as a horse, I promise you.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient presents with a single, well-systematized, circumscribed non-bizarre delusional belief that clinic staff are intentionally falsifying and altering her father's laboratory results. This fixed belief has persisted for 12 months despite repeated reassurance and contradictory evidence. Auditory and other hallucinations are absent, and functioning outside the specific domain of the delusion is completely preserved, ruling out schizophrenia and paranoid personality disorder.
